summary: Feed s176_triple to NDR is degraded: 100% VLAN tags stripped (VLANs 10,20 missing), 40.3% TCP sessions one-way, and 2.7% packet drops. NDR requires bidirectional, VLAN-aware, lossless traffic for detection - all three faults break reassembly and coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker egress is stripping 802.1Q tags - 100% of packets are untagged while NDR requires VLANs 10 and 20, indicating broker configured to strip VLAN or deliver untagged handoff to tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot segment or correlate traffic by VLAN 10/20, misses VLAN-dependent policies and detection logic, creating blind spots for those tenants.

recommended_fix.why: Preserve 802.1Q tags through packet broker to NDR so required VLAN context is retained for detection and filtering.

findings.root_cause: 85 of 211 TCP sessions (40.3%) show only one direction, typical of capturing only one side of the link or asymmetric routing where broker hashes client->server and server->client to different tool ports without aggregation.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions for TCP handshake tracking, stateful reassembly and payload analysis; one-way flows prevent session reconstruction, causing missed intrusions and broken detection.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR tool port to restore full bidirectional visibility required for stateful NDR analysis.

findings.root_cause: 68 of 2504 TCP packets (2.7%) show gaps/retransmissions indicating drops in the visibility path, most likely SPAN/mirror oversubscription and buffer exhaustion under burst since tool overload check is healthy.
findings.impact_on_tool: Missing packets break TCP reassembly, file extraction and stream analysis, degrading NDR detection accuracy and causing incomplete flows and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless full-duplex capture without SPAN buffer drops, eliminating sequence gaps and restoring complete traffic to the NDR.
